prompt:
Replace the legacy journal/ledger recovery implementation with a transactional recovery pipeline, preserving the exported APIs and standard-library-only Go 1.23 module. Use the existing domain modules, JSON/file/HTTP adapters and CLI; do not introduce a parallel ledger. The repository's 24 account files and 24 settlement journals are linked, executable fixtures. Preserve existing tests and add regression tests for the new invariants.

FRAME FORMAT. A frame is uint32 big-endian JSON payload length, exactly that many bytes of JSON encoding one Record (tags/order as types.go and encoding/json.Marshal), then uint32 big-endian IEEE CRC32 of only the payload. MaxPayload=65536, frame overhead=8. Encode accepts any Record kind/fields (semantic validation belongs to Replay) but rejects Sequence zero or oversized payload with ErrInvalid and nil bytes; output owns its storage. EncodeRecords encodes all records, requires adjacent positive sequence numbers (the first may be any positive number), rejects wraparound/gaps with ErrInvalid/nil bytes, and returns a nonnil empty byte slice for no records. Scan returns records, byte offset after the last complete valid frame, and error. At a final incomplete header (<4 bytes), payload or checksum, stop successfully at the previous offset, ignoring the torn suffix. Once four header bytes exist, advertised length zero or >MaxPayload is corrupt even if the remainder is incomplete. For complete frames, validate CRC, JSON (unknown nested/top-level fields and trailing values/garbage rejected), positive sequence, and adjacency between frames (first sequence unrestricted except nonzero). On corruption return ErrCorrupt plus the preceding records/offset, never consume the bad frame. Unknown kinds and otherwise invalid semantic fields may be scanned and are checked by Replay. No arbitrary line limits. Return nonnil empty records when empty. Do not mutate input or alias caller-owned byte/result storage.

CHECKPOINTS. Account/transaction IDs match [a-z][a-z0-9_-]*; currencies match [A-Z]{3}. Account IDs are unique, balances are nonnegative int64; closed accounts must have zero balance. NewSnapshot starts Sequence 0 with no receipts. ValidateSnapshot returns a canonical, deeply owned snapshot or zero Snapshot/ErrInvalid. Canonical means Accounts sorted by ID, Receipts sorted by Tx, both nonnil (including empty); all names/currencies/balances/closed balances valid. Receipts have unique valid Tx, unique positive commit Sequence <= snapshot.Sequence, and Digest exactly 64 lowercase hex characters. The snapshot Digest must equal lowercase SHA256 hex of encoding/json.Marshal of its canonical Snapshot with Digest set to the empty string (the digest field is present). NewSnapshot computes this digest; ValidateSnapshot verifies it. Input array order does not affect validity/digest. Arbitrary Sequence values are allowed when receipt constraints hold; no receipts are required for an aborted-only prefix. Never trust a snapshot just because its digest is syntactically well formed.

REPLAY STATE MACHINE. Replay validates the initial checkpoint first. Every record must have Sequence exactly previous+1 starting after initial.Sequence; reject uint64 wraparound, unknown kind, invalid Tx or invalid field shapes with ErrCorrupt/zero Result. begin/commit/abort require empty Account/Currency and zero Amount; open requires valid Account/Currency and zero Amount; post requires valid Account, empty Currency and NONZERO signed int64 Amount; close requires valid Account, empty Currency and zero Amount. These shape rules apply even to eventually aborted/pending transactions. begin creates an empty active transaction; beginning an already active Tx fails. open/post/close require that Tx active and append an ordered operation. Transactions may interleave. abort requires an active Tx and discards it without changing accounts/receipts; its ID may be reused. commit requires an active Tx and atomically evaluates its ordered operations against the current COMMITTED accounts at commit time, not a begin-time snapshot. open creates a previously absent account with balance 0; reopening any existing account (even closed) fails. post requires an existing open account and adds Amount to its balance. close requires an existing open account with balance exactly 0 at that operation and marks it closed permanently. Intermediate negative balances are allowed within the transaction, but every final balance must be nonnegative. Every intermediate account addition and per-currency posting-total addition must fit int64. The sum of post amounts must be zero independently for each currency, determined from the referenced account, not globally across currencies. Empty transactions and balanced multi-currency transactions are valid. Unknown accounts, nonzero currency totals, overdrafts, overflow and illegal lifecycle transitions make the entire recovery fail with ErrCorrupt.

EXACTLY ONCE. A new successful commit installs all account changes together and a Receipt. The receipt digest is lowercase SHA256 of encoding/json.Marshal of that transaction's ordered []Record operations (excluding begin/commit), with each operation's Sequence=0 and Tx=""; use a nonnil [] even for no operations. The receipt Sequence is the commit record's sequence. A Tx with an existing receipt may be begun again; at its commit compare this digest before evaluating operations against accounts. Identical operations are an idempotent replay: skip all account changes and preserve the ORIGINAL receipt/digest/commit sequence. Different digest is ErrCorrupt even if net postings match. Aborting a repeated Tx leaves the prior receipt intact.

RECOVERY AND ATOMICITY. Replay/Recover own all results and never mutate initial snapshots/records/data. Return nonnil Committed/Replayed/Discarded slices. Committed lists first-time commits in commit order, Replayed lists idempotent repeated commits in occurrence order; duplicates in Replayed are possible. Discarded is the sorted set of transactions still active at the end; their operations are abandoned, not applied or persisted. Successful State.Sequence advances through EVERY complete record, including aborted and discarded transactions; State accounts/receipts include only committed effects; refresh canonical state digest. Replay.ValidBytes is zero. Recover first validates the snapshot, then Scan, then the same replay semantics, setting ValidBytes to Scan's complete valid prefix offset; a torn suffix is allowed. Any invalid checkpoint, corrupt complete frame or invalid replay anywhere (even after earlier valid commits) returns zero Result with the appropriate ErrInvalid or ErrCorrupt and NO partial effects. NewEngine validates and owns its checkpoint; Snapshot returns owned canonical state. Engine.Recover serializes recovery, checks expected sequence first (ErrConflict takes precedence), and installs returned State only on complete success; all Engine methods are safe for concurrent use. Pending transactions do not survive a successful recovery call: the next journal starts at returned State.Sequence+1.

REPORTING. Summarize validates Result.State and returns Report: Sequence; count of all accounts, open accounts, lengths of Committed/Replayed/Discarded; Totals sorted by currency, including currencies with zero total. Totals include all accounts and must fit int64, otherwise ErrInvalid/zero Report. WriteReport calls Summarize before writing anything and emits exactly: 'sequence N\n', 'accounts A open O\n', 'transactions committed C replayed R discarded D\n', then 'CUR TOTAL\n' per currency. All output functions propagate writer errors.

INTEGRATIONS. jsonapi decoders reject unknown fields (including nested accounts/receipts/records), trailing JSON values and garbage; accept trailing whitespace and propagate reader errors. ReadSnapshot additionally validates/canonicalizes its checkpoint. JSON writers preserve supplied values and propagate errors. files.ReadSnapshot and files.Recover read their explicit paths, propagate file/JSON/domain errors, never modify files, and share the core recovery implementation. HTTP GET /snapshot ->200 canonical snapshot; GET /report ->200 Summarize(Result{State:current snapshot}), so its transaction counts are zero; POST /recover accepts RecoveryRequest (journal uses encoding/json's base64 []byte representation) and performs Engine.Recover ->200 Result. Decode/checkpoint/journal/semantic failures ->400; expected sequence conflict ->409; errors are {"error": nonempty string}; other method/path pairs ->404. API successes/errors use application/json, rejected requests leave state unchanged. app.Run accepts exactly ['encode'] (one strict JSON []Record from stdin to binary EncodeRecords output), ['checkpoint'] (one strict validated Snapshot from stdin to canonical JSON), or ['recover', snapshotPath, journalPath] / ['report', snapshotPath, journalPath] (file recovery to JSON Result / exact text report). Usage errors return 2 with stderr; runtime/decode/validation/output errors return 1 with nonempty stderr; success returns 0. Validate all input/recovery before writing stdout (output failures may naturally leave partial output); do not modify source files. CLI main must delegate to app.Run. Cover direct APIs, checkpoint restart, binary recovery, filesystem, HTTP and CLI without external services or dependencies.
